substantive_reconstruction.conjugation_and_trace: A homomorphism into GL preserves identity and inverses, including on the zero space. Multiplicativity gives phi(hgh^-1)=phi(h)phi(g)phi(h)^-1. In any commutative field tr(AB)=sum_ij A_ij B_ji=sum_ji B_ji A_ij=tr(BA). Move the invertible conjugating factor cyclically and cancel to prove similarity and conjugacy invariance. The same calculation proves basis independence. Trace linearity is a true separate property but is not an additional operation used in this argument; no averaging, finite group, metric, unitarity or semisimplicity is needed.
substantive_reconstruction.quotient_and_dimension: The definition chi_bar([g])=chi(g) is independent of representative by the proved conjugacy law. Surjectivity of the quotient-set map gives the claimed unique factorization; no finite-class assumption or infinite-group algebra-center identification is used. In an n-element basis the identity has exactly n diagonal units. For n=0 the empty sum is zero, the unique endomorphism is the zero-space identity/invertible map and the entire trace character is zero. All formula and group-law steps remain well typed.
substantive_reconstruction.field_discriminators: In characteristic zero, the natural-number scalar map is injective, since equality at n,m forces the nonzero integer n-m to vanish only when n=m. This is uniqueness of an integer encoded by a known scalar image, not an effective extraction algorithm for arbitrary field encodings. In characteristic p, the kernel of Z->K is pZ, so equality of natural scalar images is exactly congruence modulo p. For the trivial group on F_p^p the identity trace is zero despite integer dimension p. The representations on F_p and F_p^(p+1) even have the same whole constant trace character1 and distinct dimensions. These are finite, valid invertible identity actions, not a misuse of a zero matrix as an action on a nonzero space. Additional dimension bounds could restore recovery on a restricted range but are not existing premises.
